name: Linux Security Mechanism Bypass
description: Assessment and bypass of Linux mandatory access controls and security frameworks. Covers SELinux, AppArmor, and seccomp-bpf bypass techniques, namespace and cgroup escape, eBPF exploitation, Landlock circumvention, and analysis of Linux Security Module (LSM) framework internals.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to Linux security mechanism bypass

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands Linux security frameworks and mandatory access control concepts
evidence: Can explain SELinux, AppArmor, seccomp-bpf, and their enforcement models
Understands Linux namespaces, cgroups, and their role in isolation
Familiar with the LSM hook framework architecture
Completed introductory training on Linux security mechanisms

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies security mechanism configurations and tests basic bypasses under supervision
evidence: Enumerated SELinux and AppArmor policy configurations on target systems
Tested known seccomp-bpf escape techniques in lab environments
Identified overly permissive namespace configurations under guidance
Work reviewed by authorized tester

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses and bypasses Linux security mechanisms
evidence: Independently bypasses SELinux or AppArmor policies through policy weakness exploitation
Escapes seccomp-bpf sandboxes using allowed syscall chains
Exploits namespace misconfigurations for privilege boundary violations
Passed proficiency assessment on Linux security mechanism bypass

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Exploits advanced Linux security internals; develops custom bypass tooling
evidence: Exploits eBPF verifier bugs or abuses eBPF capabilities for escalation
Chains multiple namespace and cgroup escapes in complex container environments
Analyzes and bypasses Landlock and custom LSM policies
Mentors team on Linux security mechanism internals and bypass methodology

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Authority on Linux security frameworks; discovers novel bypass vectors
evidence: Published research or CVEs related to SELinux, eBPF, or LSM bypass
Developed lab methodology for Linux security mechanism assessment
Discovers novel bypass techniques in current kernel versions
Trains teams on Linux security framework internals and exploitation

assessment_methods.description: Escape from a seccomp-bpf and AppArmor-confined process on a prepared Linux host, demonstrating multiple bypass techniques
Given a SELinux policy and seccomp filter, identify exploitable weaknesses and propose escape strategies
